short: ASR decoding (M06) and phoneme LM (M07) on heard-speech ECoG: standard, with ECoG precedents of 2015. Electrodes chosen on the test set (M12); LM effect not isolated from smoothing.
position: The paper changes the decoder (M06) and language model (M07) of heard-speech ECoG decoding [@moses2016]: LDA likelihoods, a phoneme 4-gram and Viterbi search over multi-lag high-gamma windows (HGWs). Both are standard: the same ASR chain ran on ECoG of read speech in one 2015 experiment reported twice [@herff2015; @heger2015], multi-lag features predate it in the authors' group [@pasley2012], and the authors cite a same-group phone recognizer for heard multi-speaker speech (their reference 10), so their priority rests on "perceived" and "single-speaker" (§1). Against the usual design then, closed-set classification of segmented trials (8 of the 12 prior decoders with a recorded route, Appendix), open-vocabulary phoneme output is the step. The main confound for the decoding gain is its baseline: framewise estimation PERs above 100%, which the authors include "for completeness" (§3.1.1). L = 0 never won the TIMIT tuning (Table 4), but no Gump result separates the LM from HMM smoothing.
